chapter: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
title: Fletcher Henderson's stars and why big bands cannot feature everyone
summary: Asked about Louis's complaint that Henderson did not feature him, Dickenson says a big band full of stars cannot distribute solos and lists Henderson's players.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I was thinking in terms of things, for instance, like... In his later years, Louis would often say that Fletcher Henderson didn't know how to feature him right and never gave him a chance to... During that year he was with him, he never really gave him a chance to do what he felt he could do. And...

Well, that's the trouble with having a big band with a lot of stars in it. You understand? When you've got a band with a lot of stars, you try to distribute them out, you know... It makes it... You'd have to play all night long to get everybody featured. That's the trouble with being in a big band. You know? It's better to have a small band. You know? I mean that as far as the player is concerned, now. As far as the people listening, maybe they want to hear that big sound. You know? You've got to have guys that are not as ambitious, I suppose, to...
But look, Fletcher had Coleman Hawkins. He had Joe Smith. He had Buster Bailey. He had...
Not yet. Not when Louis was there.
Oh, that's right. Well, he had Charlie Green. And he had...who did he have...
